checks.claim: E1 algebra: U_(H+X)=U_H V with V driven by Z=int U_H^-1 dX U_H, in the correct LEFT order, for arbitrary bounded A including 0 and noninvertible A.
checks.reason: Formally d(U_H V)=dH U_H V+U_H dZ V=d(H+X)U_H V. There is no cross term because 2theta>1, and Young uniqueness identifies the product with U_(H+X). Then A U_(H+X)=(A U_H)V, so submultiplicativity gives the bound with V on the RIGHT and no invertibility of A. Associativity and the product rule follow from the sewing remainder and remain proof obligations, but they are not obstructions.

checks.claim: E1 uniformity: U_H, U_H^-1 and their Ctheta norms are controlled by theta,B,K only, independent of dimension, and ||Z||Ctheta<=C(theta,B,K)x.
checks.reason: Fixed-mask Section4 gives a piece count depending on K, with the local Neumann inverse and (7). The identity U^-1(t)-U^-1(s)=-U^-1(t)(U(t)-U(s))U^-1(s) gives the inverse seminorm. Taking Y_r=U_H^-1(r)(.)U_H(r) in L(B(F),B(F)) fits Friz-Hairer (4.3) with V=W=B(F), with no tensor norm involved. Since X(0)=0, x controls [X]_theta and the increment bound gives ||Z||Ctheta<=Cx.

checks.claim: E1 exponent: log||V||<=C(z+z^nu), with zero cost at zero, a small-x LINEAR term, a large-x nu term and no per-block prefactor.
checks.reason: For small z the contraction (6a) holds on all of [0,B], so ||V||<=1+Cz<=exp(Cz). For z above a threshold, about C z^nu pieces each multiply by at most 2, giving exp(Cz^nu). Accepted (7) has a prefactor C_T and a nonzero value at x=0, so it cannot be used directly on good blocks: a per-block prefactor would cost (2/B)log C_T at speed 1/delta. E1 correctly demands the refined form. The pure-nu control confirms that the linear term is required.

checks.reason: P_m and P_m^0 both carry S_F(ell_m) on the left, matching fixed-mask (9) at s=0. The interaction norm v_m enters only the exponent. No scalar solution comparison is used.

checks.claim: E2 mean-path bound ||H_m(Phi)||Ctheta<=a_m and budget delta sum a_m^r<=D_M, with true last lengths and stopped constant extension.
checks.reason: Removing sqrt(delta) from C3 (12)-(13) gives the Holder bound on the v integrand, with L^r_v norm at most G_B^2 delta^(-1/r)||T Phi||Lr(I_m). The constant C_B=G_B^2[B^(1-1/r)+B^(1-1/r-theta)] is correct because 1-1/r>theta. Since the I_m partition I up to endpoints, delta sum a_m^r=C_B^r||T Phi||Lr(I)^r<=C_B^r||T||^r M^r. Powers and the delta weight are exact, and an empty last block gives zero.

checks.claim: E2a exact same-W decomposition with Phi_delta,J=sqrt(delta)sum_(j<=J)W(e_j)e_j, including both constants, for any size of Phi_delta,J.
checks.reason: W(T_(delta,m)f)=W(P_J T f)+W(Q_J T f), and transfer linearity splits the driver. The head coefficient is E[g_delta A W(e_j)]=sqrt(delta)H_m(e_j) by the J=0 reading of C3 (12), and g_delta delta^(a/2)=sqrt(delta) is correct. D1 (8) at J=0 independently gives the same conditional mean. Both constant columns are in C3 (12). The tuple-level almost-sure identity via countable norming statistics is a proof obligation, not a blocker.

checks.claim: E2 baseline ||P_m^0(Phi)||>=1 from the constant coordinate, without density of E in F.
checks.reason: T has range in closed iE and S_F preserves iE, so pi_C H_m=0. Hence pi_C U=pi_C by (8), and pi_C P_m^0=tau(ell_m)pi_C with triangular tau. On e0=(0,1,0) the constant coordinate of the output is (1,0). The orthogonal Hilbert norm of F then gives ||P_m^0 e0||>=1. This also holds for ell_m=0, where P_m^0=I. No density of E is used.

checks.claim: E2b good/bad block inequality with constants independent of rank, J, delta, Phi and M.
checks.reason: Good block a_m<=K: E1 gives ratio<=exp(C_K(v_m+v_m^nu)). Bad block: dividing by baseline>=1 and using (7) with T=B and ||D||<=a_m+v_m gives log ratio<=c_B(1+a_m^nu)+c' v_m^nu, with c_B,c' independent of K. Taking C_K>=c' absorbs the v term. Summing positive parts bounds log max(1,z). The bound is uniform over all m, including an empty last block with arbitrary x_N.

On a_m>K>=1: 1<=K^-r a_m^r, and a_m^nu<=K^(nu-r)a_m^r because nu<r. No block count appears, and the budget gives exactly D_M(K^-r+K^(nu-r)). This respects the rare-block control, since no uniform maximum is claimed.

checks.claim: E3 uniform CM-ball negligibility with sup outside expectation, finiteness, joint Borel integrand and the stated limit order.
checks.reason: E2b-c give delta log R<=q c_B D_M(K^-r+K^(nu-r))+delta log E exp(qC_K sum(v_m+v_m^nu)). With x<=tau+tau^(1-nu)x^nu, delta n<=2/B and delta sum v^nu<=(delta n)^(1-nu/p)Y^nu, the last term is at most qC_K(2/B)tau+delta log E exp(eta Y^nu/delta), where eta=qC_K(1+tau^(1-nu))(2/B)^(1-nu/p) is independent of J. D1 (3)-(4) then give finiteness and limsup<=A_nu eta^(2/(2-nu))(C0 epsilon_J)^(2nu/(2-nu)). Order K,tau fixed; delta to 0; J to infinity; tau to 0; K to infinity closes the estimate. R>=1 gives the lower bound 0. No C(J)epsilon_J step occurs. A_nu is used only as a sufficient constant.

checks.claim: E3/E4 joint Borel measurability of the integrand on H x B0^n.
checks.reason: Phi->H_m is bounded linear at fixed delta. D->U_D is locally Lipschitz by (6b). Left multiplication by the fixed S_F(ell_m) and the operator norm are continuous, and the denominator is at least 1. So z is jointly continuous on a separable metric space, with the K(F)-based driver paths in a separable space. No random supremum is needed.

checks.claim: E4 Q_J measurability, first-chaos head independence and the conditional inequality on the bounded action cutoff.
checks.reason: X_(m,J) is the Lp limit of finite sums with coefficients W(Q_J T f_k), hence measurable in the completed sigma field of W(Q_J H_W). That family is jointly Gaussian and orthogonal to e_j, giving independence that is not based on time support. Freezing for a nonnegative jointly Borel function gives E[f(G,X)|G]=psi(G), where psi(g)=E f(g,X)<=R on sqrt(delta)|g|<=M. Each psi(g) is one number under one fixed law, so no uncountable null-set issue arises.

minor: No statement blocker was found. These notes are optional clarifications; none is a required repair.

A_m(W) in E2a is not defined locally. It should be read as A_(m_R)(W composed with T_(delta,m)), stopped at ell_m and constantly extended, which is the J=0 case of X_(m,J) before the g_delta factor. Index m also sits near mask m_R, and B, A and H are overloaded in target and controls.

E2 says x_m in B0 while E1 requires X(0)=0. B0 is described upstream only as separable little-Holder, not explicitly zero-started. Actual X_m start at zero and the flow depends only on increments, so at worst a constant changes. An explicit x_m(0)=0 would remove the mismatch.

K-independence of c_B is needed for the final K-to-infinity step. It is implied by the notation and the allowed theta/r/B dependence, and (7) delivers it, but it is not listed explicitly. C_K must also absorb the bad-block v_m^nu coefficient.
pi_C x_m=0 is not needed for E2b; only pi_C H_m=0 enters the baseline. The assumption is harmless and holds a.s. for the actual tuple by closedness of iE.
E3 says every expectation must be jointly Borel. The precise object is the jointly Borel integrand, with the expectation then a function of Phi by Tonelli.
E4 as displayed does not use E2a. E2a only identifies P_m(Phi_delta,J,X_delta,J) with the actual block for g_delta A_m(W).

Falsification text says 45 bounded left multipliers. There are 3 distinct multipliers over 15 rows, i.e. 45 checks, as the honesty file words it. The multiplier assertion is submultiplicativity after exact factorization, so it is not an independent E1 test. JSON records only the count, not row-level multiplier results.

Target line 105-106 asks new tests to exercise zero and last-block cases. The controls have only t=0 and differing t values. They do not test S_F endpoints, the pi_C baseline, or the size law x+x^nu. This is acceptable because E1-E4 do not rely on them, but it limits what the controls show.
Index convention: C3 Section4 writes sum_j<J while target and D1 use j<=J from e_1. Both mean the first J vectors; J=0 is the empty head.
Crosswalk could cite D1 (8) as an additional accepted route to E2a head regression. Fixed-mask (7) should be labelled bad-block only.

Optional proof obligations for the later full proof, not statement defects: sewing-level product rule and associativity; dimension-free inverse and conjugation bounds; refined small and large z growth; tuple-level a.s. E2a on one event; joint continuity of the flow into z; Q_J measurability through transfer limits; the freezing lemma.
